Heard on I.A.No.1/18, application for condonation of delay in filing the appeal.
2. Though opposed, looking to the reasons stated in the application, the same is allowed.
Delay of 67 days in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.

3. Admit.
4.
With the consent of the parties, the matter is heard finally.

5. This appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act of 1988') has been filed by the claimants / appellants aggrieved by award dated 28/10/2017 passed in claim case No.214/2011 by the 1 st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Balod (CG).

sentences.text: 1 Tribunal passed an award to the tune of Rs.4,49,000/- to the appellants / claimants.

6. Facts of the case in brief is that the deceased - Chhailendra Kumar died in an accident occurred on 13/08/2010 by rash and negligent driving of a truck (offending vehicle) bearing registration no.CG 04 J-9173.
The offending vehicle was driven by respondent No.1 / driver.
Claim application was filed claiming total compensation of Rs.77,60,000/- along with interest.
The claim application was resisted by the driver, owner and insurance company.

Learned Tribunal assessed the monthly income of the deceased to Rs.3,000/- and by deducting  of the personal expenses and applying multiplier of 18 awarded Rs.3,24,000/- for loss of dependency, Rs.25,000/- for funeral expenses,
Rs.1 lakh for love and affection, the total compensation awarded to the tune of Rs.4,49,000/-.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the income of the deceased has been assessed on lower side as admittedly, he was studying in the Engineering College, he definitely would have bright future.
Therefore, the monthly income ought to have been taken adequately.

Apart from this,
future prospects has not been added and the amount on other admissible heads are also on the lower side.

8. Learned counsel for the respondent / insurance company submits that the accident had occurred in the year 2010 and looking to the facts and circumstances, the finding recorded by the learned Tribunal appears to be just and reasonable.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.

10. From the records, it appears that the deceased had appeared in the professional examination and from the evidence of claimants, he was admitted in the Engineering College and pursuing his studies.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Smt. Meena Pawaia & Ors. Vs. Ashraf Ali & Ors.

entities.text: Smt. Meena Pawaia & Ors. Vs. Ashraf Ali & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 1083 while dealing with the case observed that the deceased at the time of accident was aged 21-22 years and that he was a student of 3rd year in civil engineering and observed that the deceased was studying in 3rd/4th semester of Civil Engineering, he cannot be considered worse than the labourers/skilled labourers
and enhanced the compensation in that case.
11. Considering the fact that the accident took place in the year 2010 and the deceased was studying in Engineering College, this Court assess the monthly income of the deceased to Rs.5,000/-.

12. Taking guidance from the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and ors., (2009) 6 SCC 121, National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Pranay Sethi and ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., (2018) 18 SCC 130

The learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.4,49,000/- which is deducted from the total compensation and the enhanced compensation comes to Rs.4,32,000/-.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, interest @ 6% is also awarded on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of filing of the claim application to be deposited within a period of 60 days.
After deposit, Rs.2 lakhs each shall be invested in the name of the appellants as fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in a nationalised bank.
The remainder shall be paid through bank transaction/account payee cheque.
14. The appeal thus partly allowed.
